Class JsonWriter

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.http.JsonWriter
public final class JsonWriter extends Object
Writes JSON into a caller-owned byte[], placing commas and escaping strings, so request and response bodies need no hand-written quotes. Create one writer at startup and reset() it per body: writing allocates nothing. toString() copies the body into a String for APIs that take one, such as HttpServer.respond(int, String, String) or HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString. 
JsonWriter json = new JsonWriter(new byte[64]);
json.reset().beginObject().name("uptime_ms").value(clock.millis()).name("ok").value(true).endObject();
HttpServer.respond(HttpStatus.OK, "application/json", json.toString());

Output that does not fit the buffer is dropped and overflowed() turns true. Nesting deeper than 31 levels, a name outside an object, an unbalanced close, or a NaN or infinite double (JSON has no literal for them) also mark the writer overflowed instead of throwing.
